sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片当DJ的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是瑞秋·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Over the last year, the Trump administration has dramatically changed the kinds of civil rights cases it pursues.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，特朗普政府大幅改变了其所追求的民权案件类型。

sentences.en: Gone is the focus of fighting race-based discrimination, the very purpose for which the Civil Rights Division at the Justice Department was founded.
sentences.zh: 打击基于种族的歧视这一核心重点已经不复存在，而这正是司法部民权司成立的初衷。

sentences.en: And instead, the department's focusing on things like transgender women in sports and anti-Christian bias.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是，司法部开始关注诸如跨性别女性参与体育运动以及反基督教偏见之类的问题。

sentences.en: And it's going one step further, abandoning cases already in progress.
sentences.zh: 而且他们更进一步，放弃了已经在审理中的案件。

sentences.en: Today, we want to tell you about one of those cases.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们想向大家讲述其中一个案件。

sentences.en: And to do that, we're doing something a little different.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，我们要尝试一些不同的方式。

sentences.en: We're bringing our colleague Sarah Koenig from Serial Productions to tell you the story of one woman whose civil rights case was turned upside down by these changes that we've all been seeing.
sentences.zh: 我们请来了《Serial》制作公司的同事莎拉·凯尼格，由她来讲述一位女性的故事，这位女性的民权诉讼案正是因为我们所看到的这些变化而陷入了困境。

sentences.en: It's Friday, March 13th, and here is Sarah.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月13日，星期五，下面请听莎拉的讲述。

sentences.en: A while back, I got a hold of this liSt.
sentences.zh: 不久前，我拿到了一份名单。

sentences.en: It was a rundown of all these civil rights cases that were not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 上面列出了所有即将被搁置的民权案件。

sentences.en: They'd all been dropped or set aside by the Department of Justice.
sentences.zh: 它们都被司法部撤销或搁置了。

sentences.en: And I saw one I'd never heard of.
sentences.zh: 我看到了一个我从未听说过的案件。

sentences.en: A small case, straightforward, one simple issue, easy to get your head around.
sentences.zh: 一个小案子，直截了当，只有一个简单的问题，很容易理解。

sentences.en: That's the one I want to tell you about.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想告诉你们的那个案子。

sentences.en: It's the story of a woman named Christy Metcalf.
sentences.zh: 这是一个名叫克里斯蒂·梅特卡夫的女性的故事。

sentences.en: She's the subject of the lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 她就是这起诉讼的主角。

sentences.en: Once I talked to her, I understood this small case and how it was squandered is as clear a window as any into how civil rights enforcement is operating right now.
sentences.zh: 在和她交谈后，我明白了这起小案子以及它是如何被浪费掉的，这就像一扇清晰的窗口，让我们看到了当前的民权执法是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Christy Metcalf is a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂·梅特卡夫是一位律师。

sentences.en: However, the job she does is not the flashy kind of lawyering.
sentences.zh: 然而，她所从事的工作并非那种光鲜亮丽的法律工作。

sentences.en: It's the unsung kind of lawyering.
sentences.zh: 这是一种默默无闻的法律工作。

sentences.en: Christy Metcalf drafts legislation, or at least for much of her career she did.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂负责起草立法，或者至少在她职业生涯的大部分时间里是这样。

sentences.en: When senators in the Mississippi legislature wanted to change the rules of their state, Christy wrote the bills to make that happen.
sentences.zh: 当密西西比州议会的参议员们想要修改州规时，克里斯蒂就会起草法案来实现这些目标。

sentences.en: You are nonpartisan and you work for all of the senators.
sentences.zh: 你必须保持中立，为所有的参议员服务。

sentences.en: So, I certainly had my share of drafting legislation that I personally did not agree with.
sentences.zh: 所以，我当然也起草过不少我个人并不认同的法案。

sentences.en: A lot, a lot of that.
sentences.zh: 很多，真的很多。

sentences.en: Christy would leave out her own two cents.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂会把自己的个人观点放在一边。

sentences.en: Instead, she'd explain to the senators what the Mississippi Constitution said, what the U.S.
sentences.zh: 相反，她会向参议员们解释密西西比州宪法是怎么说的，美国宪法是怎么说的，

sentences.en: Constitution said, why the thing they were proposing might not pass muster if challenged in court.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么他们提议的内容如果被诉诸法庭可能无法通过考验。

sentences.en: And a lot of times, she told me, the senators did not care.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，很多时候，参议员们根本不在乎。

sentences.en: All right, fine, whatever.
sentences.zh: 行吧，随它去，无所谓。

sentences.en: I'll draft it.
sentences.zh: 我来起草就是了。

sentences.en: But generally, did you like the work?
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，你喜欢这份工作吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 喜欢。

sentences.en: Yes, I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我喜欢。

sentences.en: She respected the process.
sentences.zh: 她尊重这个流程。

sentences.en: She had faith in its fairness.
sentences.zh: 她相信其公平性。

sentences.en: And can I just ask, I mean, this is a, the question that is hard to, maybe to answer, but were you good at it?
sentences.zh: 我能问一下吗，我的意思是，这个问题可能很难回答，但你擅长这份工作吗？

sentences.en: Like, were you good at it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你做得好吗？

sentences.en: You were.
sentences.zh: 你做得很好。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: No, that's not, I love that question because here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 不，那个问题我喜欢，因为情况是这样的。

sentences.en: I come from super middle class backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 我来自非常普通的工薪阶层背景。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Okay, so I always felt like it was important to draft legislation in a way that any person could read it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我一直觉得，起草法案时，让任何普通人都能读懂是很重要的。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: It's just useless to talk about res ipsa loquitur to a layperson.
sentences.zh: 对门外汉谈论“事实自证”（res ipsa loquitur）是毫无意义的。

sentences.en: Like, they don't care.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不在乎。

sentences.en: Like, what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 就像是，你在说什么呢？

sentences.en: This Latin stuff, like, that doesn't mean anything to me.
sentences.zh: 这些拉丁语术语，对我来说毫无意义。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, I got two degrees.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我有两个学位。

sentences.en: I got a law degree.
sentences.zh: 我拿到了法学学位。

sentences.en: I don't know what it means when you say notwithstanding as provided in.
sentences.zh: 但我也不知道当你提到“尽管有……的规定”时是什么意思。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: No, in every piece of legislation that I drafted at the request of a senator, I tried to do it in a way with my mom in mind.
sentences.zh: 不，我起草的每一份法案，都是应参议员的要求，但我尝试以我母亲的角度来撰写。

sentences.en: Can this licensed cosmetologist understand this piece of legislation that doesn't have anything to do with her actual job?
sentences.zh: 一位持证美容师能理解这份与她实际工作毫无关系的法案吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I wanted somebody that I knew, a regular person, educated or not, to be able to understand that.
sentences.zh: 我希望我认识的人，一个普通人，无论受过教育与否，都能读懂它。

sentences.en: Christy grew up in rural Alabama.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂在阿拉巴马州的农村长大。

sentences.en: As she mentioned, super middle class background.
sentences.zh: 正如她所提到的，背景非常普通。

sentences.en: Her mom worked in a manufacturing plant and later got a cosmetology license and opened the only Black-owned salon in Lamar County.
sentences.zh: 她母亲在一家制造厂工作，后来考取了美容师执照，在拉马尔县开了唯一一家由黑人经营的沙龙。

sentences.en: Her dad worked at a company that made forklift parts.
sentences.zh: 她父亲在一家生产叉车零件的公司工作。

sentences.en: She watched her many siblings go to college, then go into law enforcement or the military.
sentences.zh: 她看着自己的许多兄弟姐妹上了大学，然后进入执法部门或军队工作。

sentences.en: After Christy graduated from college, she worked at a bank for a while, saved up her money, and off she went to law school at the University of Mississippi, Ole Miss.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂大学毕业后，在银行工作了一段时间，存了些钱，然后就去密西西比大学（Ole Miss）读法学院了。

sentences.en: She scrimped to pay for it, took loans, lived in public housing, and she did what was expected of her.
sentences.zh: 她省吃俭用支付学费，申请贷款，住在公共住房里，她做了所有被期望做的事情。

sentences.en: She excelled.
sentences.zh: 她表现优异。

sentences.en: She was an editor on the Law Journal, and in 2010, she was about to graduate magna cum laude into an economy still limping from recession.
sentences.zh: 她是《法律评论》的编辑，2010年，她即将以优异成绩毕业，而当时经济仍因衰退而步履蹒跚。

sentences.en: The law firms she'd clerked out over the summers weren't hiring.
sentences.zh: 她暑期实习过的律师事务所当时都不招人。

sentences.en: She had nothing lined up.
sentences.zh: 她什么工作都没着落。

sentences.en: Her prospects were not looking good.
sentences.zh: 她的前景看起来并不乐观。

sentences.en: But Christy is not someone who folds.
sentences.zh: 但克里斯蒂不是那种会轻易放弃的人。

sentences.en: One day, the chief justice of the Mississippi Supreme Court came to speak at Ole Miss.
sentences.zh: 有一天，密西西比州最高法院的首席大法官来到密西西比大学演讲。

sentences.en: And Christy took a chance.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂抓住了一个机会。

sentences.en: After his talk, she marched up to him and asked for a clerk position.
sentences.zh: 演讲结束后，她径直走到他面前，申请了一个书记员职位。

sentences.en: The chief justice.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官。

sentences.en: That is so ballsy.
sentences.zh: 这胆子也太大了。

sentences.en: Am I allowed to say ballsy?
sentences.zh: 我能说“胆大包天”吗？

sentences.en: Like, that's really, wow.
sentences.zh: 这真的，哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And I was just, that was where I was in my life.
sentences.zh: 当时我的人生阶段就是那样。

sentences.en: I was like, I can't, I can't let this fail.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，我不能，我不能让这件事失败。

sentences.en: And the chief justice hired her.
sentences.zh: 结果首席大法官录用了她。

sentences.en: Christy loved that job.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂热爱那份工作。

sentences.en: A year later, she went on to clerk for another judge, the first African-American woman appointed to an appeals court in Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 一年后，她继续为另一位法官担任书记员，那是密西西比州上诉法院任命的第一位非裔美国女性法官。

sentences.en: And that judge had once worked for the state senate as a staff attorney.
sentences.zh: 那位法官曾经在州参议院担任过专职律师。

sentences.en: I didn't know that legislative counsel or a senate attorney, I didn't know that was a job.
sentences.zh: 我以前不知道还有立法顾问或参议院律师这种工作。

sentences.en: In undergrad, Christy had double majored in English and political science.
sentences.zh: 在本科期间，克里斯蒂主修英语和政治学双学位。

sentences.en: She loved writing.
sentences.zh: 她热爱写作。

sentences.en: She loved politics.
sentences.zh: 她热爱政治。

sentences.en: Plus, if you worked a public service job for 10 years, you could get student loan forgiveness.
sentences.zh: 另外，如果你从事公共服务工作满10年，就可以获得学生贷款减免。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, this is perfect.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，哦，这太完美了。

sentences.en: You know, can I go do this job?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我能去做这份工作吗？

sentences.en: Yes, she could, was the answer.
sentences.zh: 答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: Especially since there hadn't been a black attorney at the senate for decades.
sentences.zh: 尤其是因为几十年来参议院一直没有黑人律师。

sentences.en: And the black caucus had been agitating to rectify that.
sentences.zh: 而黑人核心小组一直在积极争取改变这一现状。

sentences.en: The senate hired young Christy Metcalfe at a salary of $55,000 a year.
sentences.zh: 参议院以每年5.5万美元的薪水聘用了年轻的克里斯蒂·梅特卡夫。

sentences.en: About five grand more than she'd been making as a judicial law clerk.
sentences.zh: 比她担任司法书记员时的收入多了大约五千美元。

sentences.en: So, to get $55,000 or whatever it was, I thought, okay, great.
sentences.zh: 所以，能拿到5.5万美元或类似的薪水，我想，好吧，太棒了。

sentences.en: I'm making more.
sentences.zh: 我赚得更多了。

sentences.en: This is great.
sentences.zh: 这太好了。

sentences.en: And I negotiated for higher than what they offered me initially.
sentences.zh: 而且我还在他们最初报价的基础上进行了协商。

sentences.en: And I thought I was on cloud nine.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得简直乐开了花。

sentences.en: You know, I just didn't.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我只是没想到。

sentences.en: What did they first offer you, do you remember?
sentences.zh: 他们最初给你开了多少钱，你还记得吗？

sentences.en: I believe it was $52,000.
sentences.zh: 我想是5.2万美元。

sentences.en: And you did the thing that, like, historically women are less good at doing or less apt to do, which is be like, uh-uh, I'm worth more than that.
sentences.zh: 你做了那件历史上女性通常不太擅长或不太愿意做的事情，那就是说：嗯-嗯，我的价值不止于此。

sentences.en: I would like some more.
sentences.zh: 我想要更多。

sentences.en: You actually did it.
sentences.zh: 你真的这么做了。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: I negotiated for more.
sentences.zh: 我争取了更高的薪水。

sentences.en: And I thought I was, I thought I was really doing something.
sentences.zh: 我当时以为，我以为我真的做了一件了不起的事。

sentences.en: Well, you were.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你确实做到了。

sentences.en: I had no idea I'm negotiating, like, $20,000 less than I should be negotiating.
sentences.zh: 我当时根本不知道我协商的薪水比我应该拿到的少了2万美元。

sentences.en: Like, they said $52,000 and you should have been like, how about $95,000?
sentences.zh: 就像是，他们说5.2万，而你本应该说，9.5万怎么样？

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because that is what the next lowest salaries were in her same office.
sentences.zh: 因为那正是她所在办公室里薪水倒数第二档的水平。

sentences.en: Which, a month later, got bumped up to $114,000.
sentences.zh: 一个月后，这个数字还涨到了11.4万美元。

sentences.en: Christy was being paid $55,000.
sentences.zh: 而克里斯蒂拿的是5.5万美元。

sentences.en: Less than half what her colleagues were getting.
sentences.zh: 不到她同事收入的一半。

sentences.en: And she knew that.
sentences.zh: 而且她知道这一点。

sentences.en: She knew she'd be making way less than everyone else before she accepted the job.
sentences.zh: 在接受这份工作之前，她就知道自己的收入会比其他人少得多。

sentences.en: She said she'd asked about it.
sentences.zh: 她说她问过这个问题。

sentences.en: When I brought it up, they said, well, salaries are based on seniority.
sentences.zh: 当我提起这件事时，他们说，嗯，薪水是根据资历定的。

sentences.en: So the longer you work here, the more you will get paid.
sentences.zh: 所以你在这里工作的时间越长，拿到的薪水就越多。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that seemed reasonable to you.
sentences.zh: 这在你看来似乎很合理。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对合理。

sentences.en: That seemed reasonable.
sentences.zh: 这看起来很合理。

sentences.en: The other lawyers, they'd all been there forever.
sentences.zh: 其他的律师，他们都在那里待了很久了。

sentences.en: 20 years.
Even 30 years.
sentences.zh: 甚至30年。

sentences.en: And here, Christy was a baby lawyer.
sentences.zh: 而克里斯蒂，只是个法律界的新手。

sentences.en: Not even two years out of law school.
sentences.zh: 法学院毕业还不到两年。

sentences.en: And the economy was crap.
sentences.zh: 而且当时经济状况很糟糕。

sentences.en: So she's not about to get greedy.
sentences.zh: 所以她并不打算贪心。

sentences.en: Then, there was this other thing.
sentences.zh: 然后，还有另一件事。

sentences.en: Another subterranean reason she accepted her roughly 50% lower salary.
sentences.zh: 她接受比别人低约50%薪水的另一个深层原因。

sentences.en: It was a saying she'd heard from her parents.
sentences.zh: 那是她从父母那里听到的一句老话。

sentences.en: From everyone around her, really.
sentences.zh: 其实是从她周围的每个人那里听到的。

sentences.en: As a Black girl growing up in the South, you're going to work twice as hard to get half as far.
sentences.zh: 作为一个在南方长大的黑人女孩，你要付出双倍的努力，才能得到一半的收获。

sentences.en: That's probably a common adage in a lot of Black households.
sentences.zh: 这在很多黑人家庭里可能是一句常见的格言。

sentences.en: It's something that I remember from even being in elementary school.
sentences.zh: 这甚至是我小学时就有的记忆。

sentences.en: Twice as hard for half as far seems like you'll never catch up.
sentences.zh: 付出双倍努力却只得到一半的回报，感觉永远也追不上。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think it was probably that for perhaps my parents.
sentences.zh: 我想我父母那辈人可能也是这样。

sentences.en: But I feel like for me, for my siblings, it has been twice as hard to get just as far.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得对于我，还有我的兄弟姐妹来说，想要达到同样的成就，确实需要付出双倍的努力。

sentences.en: Twice as hard to achieve the same thing.
sentences.zh: 实现同样的目标，却要付出双倍的艰辛。

sentences.en: Either way, the math is unfair.
sentences.zh: 不管怎么说，这笔账怎么算都不公平。

sentences.en: But for a long time, Christy didn't think of it as a problem to correct.
sentences.zh: 但很长一段时间里，克里斯蒂并没有把这看作一个需要纠正的问题。

sentences.en: A person doesn't think about pursuing her rights under the law for something that just is.
sentences.zh: 一个人不会因为某种“理所当然”的现状，就去想通过法律途径争取自己的权利。

sentences.en: Well, this is the way it's supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，事情本该如此。

sentences.en: I am supposed to work harder.
sentences.zh: 我理应更加努力。

sentences.en: I have to.
sentences.zh: 我必须这么做。

sentences.en: Christy's eventual lawsuit, as you might have guessed by now, was about equal pay.
sentences.zh: 正如你现在可能已经猜到的，克里斯蒂最终提起的诉讼，是关于同工同酬的。

sentences.en: When you read it, the stakes of her fight are obvious.
sentences.zh: 当你读到诉状时，她这场斗争的焦点显而易见。

sentences.en: Money and fairness.
sentences.zh: 金钱与公平。

sentences.en: In the complaint, those Twin Peaks are clear.
sentences.zh: 在诉状中，这两个核心诉求非常清晰。

sentences.en: What you don't see is the earthy mess below.
sentences.zh: 但你没看到的是背后那些琐碎的烂摊子。

sentences.en: All the other stuff.
sentences.zh: 所有其他的事情。

sentences.en: The muddy complications of life.
sentences.zh: 生活中那些泥泞般的复杂琐事。

sentences.en: That Christy was navigating on her slow-moving salary as the years ticked by.
sentences.zh: 随着岁月流逝，克里斯蒂就在那微薄的薪水里艰难地应对着这一切。

sentences.en: Her first four years on the job, she got a few routine raises.
sentences.zh: 入职的前四年，她得到过几次例行加薪。

sentences.en: And by January of 2016, her salary was up, from $55,000 to more than $63,000.
sentences.zh: 到2016年1月，她的薪水从55,000美元涨到了63,000多美元。

sentences.en: And she was fine with that.
sentences.zh: 她对此并无异议。

sentences.en: The job suited her.
sentences.zh: 这份工作很适合她。

sentences.en: She drafted bills for seven state senate committees, including corrections.
sentences.zh: 她为七个州参议院委员会起草法案，其中包括惩教委员会。

sentences.en: Sometimes calls would get routed to Christy from confused family members of incarcerated people.
sentences.zh: 有时，服刑人员困惑的家属打来的电话会被转接到克里斯蒂那里。

sentences.en: And she'd look their relative up on the DOC website and explain when they might get out.
sentences.zh: 她会去惩教署网站上查询他们的亲属，并解释他们何时可能获释。

sentences.en: Answering calls like that meant a lot to her.
sentences.zh: 能回答这样的电话对她来说意义重大。

sentences.en: Christy herself had a family member who'd been incarcerated.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂自己也有亲属曾入狱服刑。

sentences.en: And she saw how the uncertainty aided her mom.
sentences.zh: 她亲眼目睹了那种不确定性是如何折磨她母亲的。

sentences.en: See, that's why it's important, she thought, to have people like me in this job.
sentences.zh: 你看，她想，这就是为什么在这份工作中拥有像我这样的人很重要。

sentences.en: But the raises she got, the other senate attorneys got them too.
sentences.zh: 但她得到的加薪，其他参议院律师也同样得到了。

sentences.en: So her paycheck was still far behind.
sentences.zh: 所以她的薪水依然远远落后。

sentences.en: And yes, okay, seniority.
sentences.zh: 好吧，确实，还有资历的问题。

sentences.en: But after a while, a retort was starting to echo in Christy's head.
sentences.zh: 但过了一段时间，一个反驳的声音开始在克里斯蒂脑海中回响。

sentences.en: I am doing substantially the same job as everyone else and getting paid substantially less.
sentences.zh: 我做着和别人基本相同的工作，拿的钱却少得多。

sentences.en: She thought about asking for more money.
sentences.zh: 她想过要求加薪。

sentences.en: But 2016 turned into a swirl of medical and family crises.
sentences.zh: 但2016年却成了一场医疗和家庭危机的漩涡。

sentences.en: Christy's mother was diagnosed with cancer.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂的母亲被诊断出患有癌症。

sentences.en: Which she did not survive.
sentences.zh: 最终没能挺过去。

sentences.en: Christy reeled from the loss.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂沉浸在失去亲人的痛苦中。

sentences.en: In the months afterwards, she was having headaches.
sentences.zh: 随后的几个月里，她一直头痛。

sentences.en: Which she attributed to sadness and stress.
sentences.zh: 她把这归咎于悲伤和压力。

sentences.en: Until this one day, everything went black.
sentences.zh: 直到有一天，她眼前一黑，失去了知觉。

sentences.en: And Christy was out.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂晕倒了。

sentences.en: She remembers coming to a few days later, comically confused.
sentences.zh: 她记得几天后醒来时，那种滑稽的困惑感。

sentences.en: Asking where on earth she was.
sentences.zh: 问自己到底在哪儿。

sentences.en: What had happened on Game of Thrones.
sentences.zh: 《权力的游戏》里发生了什么。

sentences.en: And can someone hand me my bag?
sentences.zh: 还有谁能把我的包递给我？

sentences.en: I was like, where's my lipstick?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，我的口红在哪儿？

sentences.en: I need lipstick.
sentences.zh: 我需要口红。

sentences.en: And my best friend was there.
sentences.zh: 我最好的朋友当时也在场。

sentences.en: And they were like, you have a brain tumor.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你长了个脑瘤。

sentences.en: And I was like, no, I don't.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，我没有。

sentences.en: Well, not a tumor in her brain, but a tumor in her head that was pressing on her brain and that would require major surgery.
sentences.zh: 好吧，不是长在脑子里，而是长在头颅里，压迫到了大脑，需要进行大手术。

sentences.en: A craniotomy.
sentences.zh: 开颅手术。

sentences.en: Throughout all this, her mother's death, her father's subsequent decline, her own illness, her boss and colleagues at the Senate were understanding.
sentences.zh: 在这一切过程中——母亲去世、父亲随后身体每况愈下、自己患病——她在参议院的老板和同事们都非常体谅。

sentences.en: People even donated their own leave time to her so she could recover at home.
sentences.zh: 大家甚至捐出了自己的假期，好让她能在家休养。

sentences.en: In other words, this was not the time to ask for a raise.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，那并不是要求加薪的时候。

sentences.en: I just didn't see a point in that year where I could ask for that.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得那一年里没有合适的时机去提这件事。

sentences.en: I was just, I'm Southern.
sentences.zh: 我只是……我是南方人。

sentences.en: I'm polite.
sentences.zh: 我很有礼貌。

sentences.en: I don't want to cause any probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我不想惹任何麻烦。

sentences.en: I wasn't thinking about it in that manner of, this is not right.
sentences.zh: 我当时并没有从“这不公平”的角度去思考。

sentences.en: She needed this job.
sentences.zh: 她需要这份工作。

sentences.en: She still had those law school loans.
sentences.zh: 她还得偿还法学院的贷款。

sentences.en: She needed the health insurance.
sentences.zh: 她需要医疗保险。

sentences.en: She liked this job.
sentences.zh: 她喜欢这份工作。

sentences.en: And the Senate did seem to appreciate her work.
sentences.zh: 而且参议院似乎也认可她的工作。

sentences.en: And it also seemed aware that she was underpaid.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来他们也意识到她薪水过低。

sentences.en: In 2017, she got a bigger raise, a 10 percent raise.
sentences.zh: 2017年，她获得了一次幅度更大的加薪，涨了10%。

sentences.en: And then another 10 percent raise a year and a half later.
sentences.zh: 一年半后，又涨了10%。

sentences.en: Her salary is now up to $77,000.
sentences.zh: 她的年薪现在涨到了77,000美元。

sentences.en: So she thinks, maybe they're going to make this right on their own, without me having to complain.
sentences.zh: 所以她想，也许他们会主动纠正这一点，不用我再去抱怨。

sentences.en: But things quickly changed.
sentences.zh: 但情况很快发生了变化。

sentences.en: In 2018, one of the longtime Senate attorneys retired.
sentences.zh: 2018年，一位资深的参议院律师退休了。

sentences.en: The committee assignments got shuffled around so that now Christy would be responsible for drafting legislation for 10 committees out of 30 total.
sentences.zh: 委员会的工作分配进行了调整，克里斯蒂现在要负责30个委员会中10个委员会的立法起草工作。

sentences.en: She didn't have the most demanding ones, finance, judiciary, appropriations.
sentences.zh: 她负责的不是那些最繁重的，比如财政、司法或拨款委员会。

sentences.en: But still, 10 committees is a lot, about twice as many as a couple of the other attorneys.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，10个委员会也很多了，大约是其他几位律师工作量的两倍。

sentences.en: The Senate hired an attorney to replace the guy who left.
sentences.zh: 参议院雇了一名律师来接替离职的那位。

sentences.en: He was the first new hire since Christy, seven years earlier.
sentences.zh: 他是克里斯蒂七年前入职以来的第一位新员工。

sentences.en: And this new hire, a white guy, was going to be paid, you guessed it, more than Christy.
sentences.zh: 而这位新员工，一个白人男性，薪水——你猜对了——比克里斯蒂高。

sentences.en: His salary would be $101,500.
sentences.zh: 他的年薪将达到101,500美元。

sentences.en: This was Christy's last straw.
sentences.zh: 这是压垮克里斯蒂的最后一根稻草。

sentences.en: In November, she complained.
sentences.zh: 11月，她提出了申诉。

sentences.en: She went to the Director of Legislative Services, to the Secretary of the Senate, and to the Senate President Pro Tem, a guy named Terry Burton.
sentences.zh: 她找到了立法服务部主任、参议院秘书，以及参议院临时议长，一个叫特里·伯顿的人。

sentences.en: They tossed out a bunch of reasons why the new hire's salary was going to be higher than hers.
sentences.zh: 他们抛出了一堆理由，解释为什么新人的薪水会比她高。

sentences.en: Well, he's highly qualified.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他资历很高。

sentences.en: He went to a top 10 law school.
sentences.zh: 他毕业于排名前十的法学院。

sentences.en: He did, UVA.
sentences.zh: 确实，弗吉尼亚大学。

sentences.en: He was taking a pay cut to come to the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他是降薪来到参议院的。

sentences.en: He was older, so he needed more money to make this transition.
sentences.zh: 他年纪大一些，所以需要更多的钱来完成这次过渡。

sentences.en: He'd been out of law school for close to 20 years.
sentences.zh: 他从法学院毕业已经快20年了。

sentences.en: And he had a Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 而且他还有博士学位。

sentences.en: Yes, they said he had a Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们说他有博士学位。

sentences.en: He went to a great law school, you know, and then they said again, he's got a Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 他毕业于名牌法学院，你知道的，然后他们又说了一遍，他有博士学位。

sentences.en: One afternoon, not long after that conversation, Christy's suddenly summoned to a meeting with Senator Burton, whose rules committee approved salaries for Senate staff.
sentences.zh: 那天下午，那次谈话后不久，克里斯蒂突然被召去参加一个会议，与会者包括伯顿参议员，他的规则委员会负责批准参议院工作人员的薪资。

sentences.en: She goes into his office thinking it's just going to be her and Senator Burton, but three other Senate people are in there, too.
sentences.zh: 她走进办公室，以为只有她和伯顿参议员，但里面还有其他三名参议院的工作人员。

sentences.en: Feels to her like an ambush.
sentences.zh: 她感觉像中了埋伏。

sentences.en: Like the purpose of this meeting isn't to make things right.
sentences.zh: 感觉这次会议的目的根本不是为了解决问题。

sentences.en: It's to quell her complaint.
sentences.zh: 而是为了压制她的抱怨。

sentences.en: Terry Burton did most of the talking.
sentences.zh: 特里·伯顿说了大部分的话。

sentences.en: He said that he was offended and mad that it got out that the new attorney was going to be paid more than what I was being paid.
sentences.zh: 他说他感到被冒犯了，而且很生气，因为新律师的薪水比我高这件事传了出去。

sentences.en: That it was unfair, he said, to the new attorney.
sentences.zh: 他说，这对新律师不公平。

sentences.en: Senate salaries are public, but the new guys hadn't been published yet.
sentences.zh: 参议院的薪资是公开的，但新人的薪资还没公布。

sentences.en: To be clear, Christy had nothing against the particular guy who was hired and nothing against Ph.Ds.
sentences.zh: 需要说明的是，克里斯蒂对这位新来的同事没有任何意见，对博士学位也没有偏见。

sentences.en: And I think it's wonderful that somebody has a Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有人拥有博士学位是很棒的事情。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 那太了不起了。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 那很好。

sentences.en: But it doesn't have anything to do with what we do as Senate attorneys.
sentences.zh: 但这与我们作为参议院律师所做的工作毫无关系。

sentences.en: And I told them that.
sentences.zh: 我当时就是这么告诉他们的。

sentences.en: Especially when your Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当你的博士论文题目是《统治与共融：教父神学与人类与动物创造关系伦理》时。

sentences.en: thesis is titled Dominion and Communion, Patristic Theology and the Ethics of Humanity's Relationship with Animal Creation.
sentences.zh: 是的，他拿到法律学位的时间比克里斯蒂早八年，但实际上他从事法律工作的时间和她差不多长。

sentences.en: And yes, he had gotten his law degree eight years earlier than Christy, but he'd been actually practicing law for about the same amount of time as she had.
sentences.zh: 而且，至关重要的是，他没有任何起草立法的经验。

sentences.en: And, crucially, he had no experience drafting legislation.
sentences.zh: 零经验。

sentences.en: Zero.
sentences.zh: 事实上，为了培训这位新人，他们还留用了本该被他取代的那位律师，让他兼职工作。

sentences.en: In fact, to train this new hire, they were keeping on, part-time, the attorney he was supposed to replace.
sentences.zh: 后来，她也被要求参与培训新人。

sentences.en: Later, she, too, would be asked to pitch in on training the new guy.
sentences.zh: 会议上，特里·伯顿要求她给予理解。

sentences.en: In the meeting, Terry Burton was asking for her understanding.
sentences.zh: 但她并不买账。

sentences.en: But she wasn't giving it to him.
sentences.zh: 她认为他们的理由一个都站不住脚。

sentences.en: She didn't think any of their reasons held water.
sentences.zh: 这不公平。

sentences.en: This was not fair.
sentences.zh: 而且以前的工作方式也不是这样的。

sentences.en: And this was not how things had operated before.
sentences.zh: 嗯，听起来好像以前的工作方式就是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, it sounds kind of like it was how things had operated before, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你一直以来的薪水都比别人低得多。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole time you're being paid significantly less than anybody else.
sentences.zh: 我说不是，因为在我任职参议院期间，我一直被告知薪水是基于工作年限的。

sentences.en: I say that it's not because throughout my tenure with the Senate, I was told your salary is based on years of experience.
sentences.zh: 我被反复告知这一点。

sentences.en: I was told that over and over again.
sentences.zh: 所以如果不是因为资历，那是因为什么？

sentences.en: So if it wasn't about seniority, then what was it about?
sentences.zh: 显然，她不是没想过歧视的问题。

sentences.en: It's not like discrimination hadn't occurred to her, obviously.
sentences.zh: 她是黑人，女性，还有健康问题。

sentences.en: She's Black, female, had medical issues.
sentences.zh: 她一生都在阿拉巴马州和密西西比州度过。

sentences.en: She'd spent her life in Alabama and Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 她认为自己可能成为目标，这并不牵强。

sentences.en: It wasn't a stretch for her to believe she could be a target.
sentences.zh: 之前确实发生过一些不愉快的事情。

sentences.en: There had been some unpleasantness before.
sentences.zh: 例如，她告诉我有一位同事，克里斯蒂记得他说过类似这样的话：

sentences.en: She told me about one colleague, for instance, who Chrissy remembered saying stuff like,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我祖母过去常称黑人女性为“黑鬼”。

sentences.en: Well, my grandmother used to call Black women negresses.
sentences.zh: 她就是有那种本事，说：“嗯，我家里有人说过那个N开头的词。”

sentences.en: She just had a knack for saying, well, these were people in my family who said the N-word.
sentences.zh: “而且这是他们说那个词时的语境。”

sentences.en: And this was the context in which they said it.
sentences.zh: 这没问题吗？

sentences.en: Is that okay?
sentences.zh: 答案永远是否定的。

sentences.en: And the answer is always no.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，你怎么会是第一个让我遇到、却不知道这不妥的人？

sentences.en: And I was like, how am I the first person that you're meeting who's telling you that this is not okay?
sentences.zh: 但我忍了，因为我觉得他们不习惯与有色人种共事。

sentences.en: But I dealt with it because I think they were not used to working with somebody of color.
sentences.zh: 他们只是……他们不知道。

sentences.en: And they just, they didn't know.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂对这种情况采取了最宽容的态度。

sentences.en: Christy took the most generous view a person could take in this situation.
sentences.zh: 她想，这只是个人的冒犯。

sentences.en: This is an individual offense, she thought.
sentences.zh: 不是系统性的问题。

sentences.en: Not a systemic one.
sentences.zh: 我能应付。

sentences.en: I can handle it.
sentences.zh: 当然，她和同事们确实没什么共同点。

sentences.en: And sure, she didn't have much in common with her colleagues.
sentences.zh: 他们年纪较大，是白人，而且大多是男性。

sentences.en: They were older, white, and mostly men.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这正是密西西比州立法机构的真实写照。

sentences.en: An accurate reflection, in fact, of the Mississippi legislature itself.
sentences.zh: 这确实反映了密西西比州立法机构的现状。

sentences.en: But generally, she got along just fine with them.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，她和他们相处得还不错。

sentences.en: She said she'd never had to complain about her work.
sentences.zh: 她说她从未对自己的工作有过任何抱怨。

sentences.en: Her committees seemed to value her expertise.
sentences.zh: 她所在的委员会似乎很看重她的专业能力。

sentences.en: That said, Christy knew she wasn't the only Senate employee who felt intentionally underpaid.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，克里斯蒂知道她并不是唯一一个感到被蓄意压低薪资的参议院员工。

sentences.en: She knew or knew of at least three other Black people, all women, who'd complained of the same.
sentences.zh: 她认识或听说过至少还有三位黑人，全都是女性，她们也抱怨过同样的情况。

sentences.en: Back in 2013, one woman had even sued in federal court unsuccessfully.
sentences.zh: 早在2013年，甚至有一位女性在联邦法院起诉过，但没能成功。

sentences.en: This situation, though, with the new hire, this was not working twice as hard to get just as far in a way Christy could live with.
sentences.zh: 然而，这次新员工入职的情况，却不是克里斯蒂所能接受的那种“付出双倍努力才能获得同等回报”。

sentences.en: Is that when you started to think like, oh, I see, this is racial discrimination.
sentences.zh: 那是你开始觉得，噢，我明白了，这是种族歧视的时候吗？

sentences.en: I thought this was something else, but I'm seeing it now?
sentences.zh: 我以为这是别的原因，但我现在看明白了？

sentences.en: Or did you know, did you feel like that all along?
sentences.zh: 还是说你一直以来都有这种感觉？

sentences.en: You're like, they're doing this to me because I'm a Black woman and they feel like they can.
sentences.zh: 你当时觉得，他们这样对我，是因为我是黑人女性，而且他们觉得他们可以这么做。

sentences.en: I felt like it somewhat before, but it became very apparent when they hired a white male and paid him $24,000 more than what I was being paid.
sentences.zh: 我之前就有过这种感觉，但当他们雇佣了一名白人男性，且薪水比我高出24,000美元时，这一点就变得非常明显了。

sentences.en: Like, it's undeniable at that point.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，这简直是无可辩驳的。

sentences.en: Terry Burton did not want to talk to me for this story, so I don't have his version of events.
sentences.zh: 特里·伯顿不想就这个故事接受我的采访，所以我没有他那边的说法。

sentences.en: But I was able to interview someone who worked in the same office as Christy, a longtime Senate attorney named Larry Richardson.
sentences.zh: 但我采访到了和克里斯蒂在同一个办公室工作的人，一位在参议院工作多年的律师，拉里·理查森。

sentences.en: I explained to Larry how, in the beginning, the huge pay discrepancy made sense to Christy.
sentences.zh: 我向拉里解释了起初巨大的薪资差距在克里斯蒂看来是合理的。

sentences.en: She said, well, I was told it was all based on seniority.
sentences.zh: 她说，嗯，有人告诉我这完全是基于资历。

sentences.en: Larry Richardson had retired by the time the new guy was hired, so he wasn't there for the aftermath.
sentences.zh: 拉里·理查森在新员工入职时已经退休了，所以他不在现场，不知道后续发生的事。

sentences.en: But he told me he'd been agitating for years over what he saw as unfair pay for Senate staff.
sentences.zh: 但他告诉我，多年来他一直对参议院员工薪酬不公的问题感到不满。

sentences.en: He said the seniority thing?
sentences.zh: 他说资历那一套？

sentences.en: That's BS.
sentences.zh: 那是胡扯。

sentences.en: He said he'd collected all this data, which he'd eventually presented to the Rules Committee,
sentences.zh: 他说他收集了所有这些数据，并最终提交给了规则委员会，

sentences.en: showing how other legislative employees were better paid than Senate attorneys, for no good reason.
sentences.zh: 展示了其他立法机构员工的薪水如何比参议院律师更高，而且毫无正当理由。

sentences.en: But even if salaries were based on seniority, Larry said Christy's pay gap specifically made no sense to him.
sentences.zh: 但拉里说，即使薪水是基于资历，克里斯蒂的薪资差距对他来说也完全说不通。

sentences.en: First of all, if you start someone that low, at $55,000, and everyone's getting raises along the way...
sentences.zh: 首先，如果你起薪给得那么低，只有55,000美元，而其他人都在涨工资……

sentences.en: She will never catch up.
sentences.zh: 她永远也追不上。

sentences.en: You see the problem.
sentences.zh: 你明白问题所在了。

sentences.en: And then to hire the new guy for way more money?
sentences.zh: 然后又以高得多的薪水雇佣了那个新人？

sentences.en: He said he was flabbergasted when he saw that.
sentences.zh: 他说他看到那个的时候简直惊呆了。

sentences.en: There was no reason for that kind of disparity.
sentences.zh: 那种差距根本没有任何理由。

sentences.en: Just based on qualifications, work, she knew the Senate rules.
sentences.zh: 单从资历和工作来看，她很了解参议院的规则。

sentences.en: Christy met with her committees, showed up on the floor.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂会参加委员会会议，也会出席议会现场。

sentences.en: Even when her close family had serious health problems and then she herself had been sick,
sentences.zh: 即使在她直系亲属有严重的健康问题，甚至她自己也生病的时候，

sentences.en: Larry didn't recall anyone having to cover for her.
sentences.zh: 拉里不记得有人需要替她分担工作。

sentences.en: Now, I never heard any complaints.
sentences.zh: 我从未听到过任何抱怨。

sentences.en: And I would have heard them.
sentences.zh: 而且我肯定会听到的。

sentences.en: But no, I never heard any complaints about her work.
sentences.zh: 但没有，我从未听到过任何关于她工作的抱怨。

sentences.en: But you also didn't hear any gossip or something of, like, that new girl is really a pain in the butt or something.
sentences.zh: 但你也没有听到过任何流言蜚语，比如“那个新来的女孩真是个麻烦精”之类的。

sentences.en: No one was...
sentences.zh: 没有人……

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: She did the job, Larry said, and people seemed to like her.
sentences.zh: 拉里说，她完成了工作，而且人们似乎很喜欢她。

sentences.en: As to whether racial discrimination might have been the reason Christy was paid less,
sentences.zh: 至于种族歧视是否可能是克里斯蒂薪水较低的原因，

sentences.en: Larry couldn't say.
sentences.zh: 拉里无法断言。

sentences.en: But he did work at the legislature for 37 years.
sentences.zh: 但他确实在立法机构工作了37年。

sentences.en: So he offered a general assessment.
sentences.zh: 所以他给出了一个总体的评价。

sentences.en: The Senate just historically has been white.
sentences.zh: 参议院在历史上一直都是白人的天下。

sentences.en: In that meeting Christy had with Senator Terry Burton, she said he told her something she found odd.
sentences.zh: 在克里斯蒂与参议员特里·伯顿的那次会面中，她说他告诉了她一件她觉得奇怪的事。

sentences.en: He said the Senate wasn't bound by any Mississippi state personnel rules or regulations.
sentences.zh: 他说参议院不受任何密西西比州人事规则或条例的约束。

sentences.en: Or any rules.
sentences.zh: 或者说不受任何规则约束。

sentences.en: They didn't have to follow anything regarding pay, posting jobs on the website, or setting formal standards for job qualifications.
sentences.zh: 他们在薪酬、网站招聘或设定正式的任职资格标准方面不需要遵循任何规定。

sentences.en: He said the Senate can, quote,
sentences.zh: 他说参议院可以，引用原话：

sentences.en: do what it wants, unquote.
sentences.zh: “想做什么就做什么”。

sentences.en: Christy thought, but there's a whole federal law that says you shouldn't do this.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂心想，但有一整部联邦法律规定你们不应该这样做。

sentences.en: That federal law is known as Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which says an employer cannot discriminate against someone based on their race, sex, religion, etc.
sentences.zh: 那部联邦法律就是1964年《民权法案》第七章，规定雇主不得基于种族、性别、宗教等原因歧视他人。

sentences.en: Christy could have filed a Title VII complaint right away with the EEOC, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission,
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂本可以立即向平等就业机会委员会（EEOC）提交第七章投诉，

sentences.en: the federal agency that investigates workplace discrimination claiMs.
sentences.zh: 这是一个调查职场歧视索赔的联邦机构。

sentences.en: Instead, she waited.
sentences.zh: 但她选择了等待。

sentences.en: She told me she just didn't believe that in their collective Senate heart, anyone thought this pay discrepancy was truly okay.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，她只是不相信在参议院的集体心中，真的有人觉得这种薪资差距是没问题的。

sentences.en: Surely they'd correct it on their own.
sentences.zh: 他们肯定会自行纠正的。

sentences.en: Three months went by.
sentences.zh: 三个月过去了。

sentences.en: Five months.
sentences.zh: 五个月过去了。

sentences.en: Nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有发生。

sentences.en: Christy's part of an organization that mentors young women.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂所在的组织致力于指导年轻女性。

sentences.en: She was always telling them, you have to stand up for yourself.
sentences.zh: 她总是告诉她们，你们必须为自己挺身而出。

sentences.en: That women are important.
sentences.zh: 女性很重要。

sentences.en: Black women are important.
sentences.zh: 黑人女性很重要。

sentences.en: You need to run for office.
sentences.zh: 你们需要竞选公职。

sentences.en: You need to get involved in your political environment.
sentences.zh: 你们需要参与到政治环境中去。

sentences.en: Your voice matters.
sentences.zh: 你们的声音很重要。

sentences.en: And I felt like I'm a hypocrite if I don't move forward with this.
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果我不采取行动，我就是一个伪君子。

sentences.en: There was a statutory time limit for Christy to file with the EEOC.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂向EEOC提交投诉有法定的时间限制。

sentences.en: So if she was going to do it, it was now or never.
sentences.zh: 所以如果她要这么做，现在就是最后的机会。

sentences.en: I went and filed that, I filed that complaint.
sentences.zh: 我去了，提交了那份投诉。

sentences.en: After the break, Sarah Koenig returns with the rest of Christy's story.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，莎拉·凯尼格将带着克里斯蒂故事的后续回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.zh: 现在订阅即可在 nytimes.com/subscribe 享受特别优惠。

sentences.en: Once Christy Metcalf filed her complaint with the Equal Opportunity Employment Commission, alleging
sentences.zh: 当克里斯蒂·梅特卡夫向平等就业机会委员会提交投诉，声称

sentences.en: discrimination was the reason for her low salary, she figured it was a no-brainer.
sentences.zh: 歧视是她低薪的原因时，她认为这显而易见。

sentences.en: They'll see they violated federal law.
sentences.zh: 他们会看到他们违反了联邦法律。

sentences.en: They'll fix it.
sentences.zh: 他们会改正的。

sentences.en: If for no other reason than to get me to shut up about it.
sentences.zh: 就算没有别的理由，至少为了让我闭嘴，他们也会改正。

sentences.en: Instead, as the EEOC investigated, the Mississippi Senate dug in.
sentences.zh: 然而，随着EEOC的调查，密西西比州参议院却坚持己见。

sentences.en: They never claimed Christy had done anything wrong at work or wasn't good at her job.
sentences.zh: 他们从未声称克里斯蒂在工作中做错了什么，或者工作能力不行。

sentences.en: Instead, they argued that the new guy was getting more money because his job working with the
sentences.zh: 相反，他们辩称那个新人薪水更高，是因为他从事的与

sentences.en: finance committee required more, quote, skill, effort, and responsibility than Christy's.
sentences.zh: 财务委员会相关的工作比克里斯蒂的需要更多的“技能、努力和责任”。

sentences.en: When the EEOC didn't buy that, the Senate argued instead that she wasn't a protected employee under Title VII.
sentences.zh: 当EEOC不买账时，参议院又辩称她不是第七章保护下的员工。

sentences.en: Christy couldn't afford to hire a lawyer to represent her side in the EEOC case, so she did it herself, referring to herself in the third person.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂负担不起聘请律师在EEOC案件中代表她，所以她亲自上阵，以第三人称称呼自己。

sentences.en: Metcalf contends that there is direct evidence, etc.
sentences.zh: 梅特卡夫主张存在直接证据，等等。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, working at the Senate was becoming intolerable.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在参议院的工作变得令人无法忍受。

sentences.en: She and her fellow attorneys had always worked well together before, helped each other out.
sentences.zh: 她和同事们以前一直合作得很好，互相帮助。

sentences.en: But now her colleagues stopped talking to her.
sentences.zh: 但现在她的同事们不再和她说话了。

sentences.en: She said she learned later they'd been told to, quote, limit contact.
sentences.zh: 她说她后来才知道他们被告知要“限制接触”。

sentences.en: Gossip would float back to her.
sentences.zh: 流言蜚语传到了她耳中。

sentences.en: Oh, she filed an EEOC complaint.
sentences.zh: 噢，她提交了EEOC投诉。

sentences.en: If she's so unhappy, why doesn't she just leave?
sentences.zh: 如果她那么不开心，为什么不直接辞职呢？

sentences.en: Other attorneys would drop their bills on her desk to finish.
sentences.zh: 其他律师会把账单扔在她的桌子上让她完成。

sentences.en: In the past, you might offer to pitch in and a crunch, but this felt different, like she was being punished.
sentences.zh: 过去，你可能会在紧急关头主动帮忙，但这感觉不同，就像她在受惩罚一样。

sentences.en: I kind of became the repository for bills that no other attorney wanted to draft.
sentences.zh: 我几乎成了其他律师不想起草的账单的收容所。

sentences.en: And I was generally just cut out of the general conversations that would happen amongst
sentences.zh: 而且我基本上被排除在了律师们之间进行的日常对话之外，

sentences.en: the attorneys, and during this time, I started second-guessing my decision to foul the charge, because I was afraid of being blackballed.
sentences.zh: 在这期间，我开始质疑自己提交指控的决定，因为我害怕被列入黑名单。

sentences.en: And I kept thinking, well, this is it.
sentences.zh: 我一直想，好吧，就是这样了。

sentences.en: I've made this wrong decision, and I'm going to ruin it for any other black woman who might want to work here, and they're not going to consider her.
sentences.zh: 我做出了错误的决定，我将毁掉任何可能想在这里工作的黑人女性的机会，他们不会考虑她们的。

sentences.en: And I put a lot of this pressure on myself and was just—I was having a very, very tough time, and I didn't have
sentences.zh: 我给自己施加了很大的压力，我当时正经历着非常非常艰难的时刻，而且我没有

sentences.en: anyone else who had been in a similar situation to really even
sentences.zh: 任何处于类似处境的人可以真正地

sentences.en: talk to about this.
sentences.zh: 谈论这件事。

sentences.en: Her relationship with her husband and her stepkids was suffering from all this, too.
sentences.zh: 她与丈夫和继子女的关系也因此受到了影响。

sentences.en: He'd been pushing her for a while to leave this job that didn't seem to value her, that
sentences.zh: 他一直催促她离开这份似乎不重视她的工作，这份工作

sentences.en: kept them living apart during the work week, she in Jackson, he in Columbus, a two-and-a-half-hour drive each way.
sentences.zh: 让他们在工作周期间分居两地，她在杰克逊，他在哥伦布，单程车程两个半小时。

sentences.en: Christy's mental health got so bad, she felt like she was at a breaking point.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂的心理健康状况变得非常糟糕，她觉得自己到了崩溃的边缘。

sentences.en: About five months after she filed the EEOC complaint, she quit.
sentences.zh: 在提交EEOC投诉约五个月后，她辞职了。

sentences.en: The EEOC did its thing.
sentences.zh: EEOC做了它该做的事。

sentences.en: Investigators interviewed people at the Senate, combed through the documentation.
sentences.zh: 调查人员采访了参议院的人，仔细查阅了文件。

sentences.en: What they were looking for, in part, is whether they can find any non-discriminatory reason to explain the disparity in Christy's pay.
sentences.zh: 他们寻找的，部分是为了看能否找到任何非歧视性的理由来解释克里斯蒂的薪资差距。

sentences.en: Seniority say, that's a valid, non-discriminatory reason.
sentences.zh: 比如资历，那是一个正当的、非歧视性的理由。

sentences.en: Or lesser qualifications.
sentences.zh: 或者资历较浅。

sentences.en: Or lousy job performance.
sentences.zh: 或者工作表现糟糕。

sentences.en: They could not find anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么也没找到。

sentences.en: About two years after she filed her claim, the EEOC made its determination.
sentences.zh: 在她提交索赔约两年后，EEOC做出了裁定。

sentences.en: And it sided with Christy.
sentences.zh: 它站在了克里斯蒂这一边。

sentences.en: The EEOC said there was, quote, reasonable cause to believe that the Mississippi Senate paid Christy Metcalfe disparate wages because of her race, in violation of Title VII.
sentences.zh: EEOC表示，有“合理理由相信密西西比州参议院因种族原因向克里斯蒂·梅特卡夫支付了不平等的工资，违反了第七章”。

sentences.en: The EEOC tried to settle the claim.
sentences.zh: EEOC试图调解此案。

sentences.en: Christy wouldn't sue the Senate if they'd agree to stop discriminating.
sentences.zh: 如果参议院同意停止歧视，克里斯蒂就不会起诉他们。

sentences.en: And they'd need to develop and implement policies prohibiting retaliation, and train staff on those policies.
sentences.zh: 他们需要制定并实施禁止报复的政策，并对员工进行相关政策培训。

sentences.en: And they'd need to pay Christy more than $200,000 in back pay and damages.
sentences.zh: 他们还需要支付克里斯蒂超过20万美元的补发工资和赔偿金。

sentences.en: The Senate came back with a counteroffer.
sentences.zh: 参议院提出了反建议。

sentences.en: How about we don't do any of that?
sentences.zh: 我们什么都不做怎么样？

sentences.en: And instead we pay Christy $5,000.
sentences.zh: 我们只付给克里斯蒂5,000美元。

sentences.en: And we invite her to never apply to work here ever again.
sentences.zh: 并且我们邀请她永远不要再申请来这里工作。

sentences.en: How about that?
sentences.zh: 这样如何？

sentences.en: This was playing out in legalese, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这都是在法律术语中进行的博弈。

sentences.en: Now Christy wrote back from the heart.
sentences.zh: 现在克里斯蒂发自内心地写了回信。

sentences.en: In first person.
sentences.zh: 用第一人称。

sentences.en: She read it aloud for me.
sentences.zh: 她大声读给我听。

sentences.en: The emotional stress that the Senate's pay discrimination caused has wrecked my life.
sentences.zh: 参议院的薪酬歧视所造成的情绪压力摧毁了我的生活。

sentences.en: The stress of knowing they were paying me less to do the same job as another employee also seeped into my home and marriage.
sentences.zh: 知道他们因为我做着和另一名员工同样的工作却付给我更少的薪水，这种压力也渗透到了我的家庭和婚姻中。

sentences.en: I felt like I had...
sentences.zh: 我觉得我……

sentences.en: She'd sought help from more than one therapist, she wrote.
sentences.zh: 她写道，她曾向不止一位治疗师寻求帮助。

sentences.en: Her husband had filed for divorce, ending her contact with her stepkids.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫提出了离婚，这切断了她与继子女的联系。

sentences.en: By now, it was year two of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 当时已经是疫情的第二年了。

sentences.en: She had a hard time finding work.
sentences.zh: 她很难找到工作。

sentences.en: For a while, she worked as a leasing agent for an apartment complex, where she'd clean the units before showing them to prospective renters.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，她在一家公寓大楼做租赁代理，在带潜在租客看房前，她得负责打扫单元房。

sentences.en: When she thinks of it now, cat shit comes to mind.
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，她脑子里浮现出的就是猫屎。

sentences.en: She eventually started managing the place in exchange for discounted rent.
sentences.zh: 后来她开始管理那栋楼，以此换取房租减免。

sentences.en: The hardest job of her life, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，这是她这辈子做过最辛苦的工作。

sentences.en: When she finally got an attorney position, it was at Child Protective Services.
sentences.zh: 当她终于得到一份律师职位时，是在儿童保护服务局。

sentences.en: But it practically killed her.
sentences.zh: 但这简直要了她的命。

sentences.en: How depressing it was.
sentences.zh: 那段日子太压抑了。

sentences.en: The EEOC and the Mississippi Senate could not come to an agreement about how to solve Christy's case.
sentences.zh: 美国平等就业机会委员会（EEOC）和密西西比州参议院无法就如何解决克里斯蒂的案件达成一致。

sentences.en: So the EEOC called it quits.
sentences.zh: 于是EEOC放弃了。

sentences.en: Passed the case along to the Department of Justice.
sentences.zh: 把案子移交给了司法部。

sentences.en: Saying, essentially, we think there's been discrimination here.
sentences.zh: 基本上是说，我们认为这里存在歧视。

sentences.en: Do what you will.
sentences.zh: 你们看着办吧。

sentences.en: Christy's case landed in the Civil Rights Division of the DOJ.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂的案子落到了司法部民权司的手里。

sentences.en: In the section that litigates employment discrimination, where they don't mess around.
sentences.zh: 在那个专门负责诉讼就业歧视的部门，他们可不是吃素的。

sentences.en: They only pick fights they're fairly certain they can win.
sentences.zh: 他们只打那些有把握赢的官司。

sentences.en: And Christy's case made the cut.
sentences.zh: 而克里斯蒂的案子入选了。

sentences.en: It was chosen not just for investigation, but eventually for litigation.
sentences.zh: 它不仅被选中进行调查，最终还被选中进行诉讼。

sentences.en: An even higher bar.
sentences.zh: 这门槛更高了。

sentences.en: In late 2024, more than five years after Christy had made her initial complaint, the DOJ filed a lawsuit on her behalf.
sentences.zh: 2024年底，在克里斯蒂最初投诉五年多后，司法部代表她提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: After the cancer and your mom dying and the tumor in your head and the meanness and the divorce and the cat shit and the child abuse evidence you can't unsee.
sentences.zh: 经历了癌症、母亲去世、脑部肿瘤、刻薄的对待、离婚、猫屎，还有那些让你无法忘怀的虐童证据。

sentences.en: What was that like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: I remember.

sentences.zh: 莎拉，我觉得这对我个人来说是一个巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: But more importantly, for the other women who worked for the Senate, because they had worked there longer than I did, you know?
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，这对其他在参议院工作的女性来说也是，因为她们在那里工作的时间比我长，你懂吗？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.zh: 她们也处理过这些情况，但当她们向规则委员会提出时却被无视了，

sentences.en: Committee, I thought that meant that what I was arguing was justified, and they saw a point in all of it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这意味着我的主张是正当的，他们也看到了其中的意义。

sentences.en: And I thought it was huge.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这意义重大。

sentences.en: I thought that people would say, this is a slam dunk.
sentences.zh: 我以为大家会说，这简直是稳操胜券。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I don't know how other attorneys feel with what they have contributed to the legal profession,
sentences.zh: 我不知道其他律师对自己为法律界所做的贡献有何感想，

sentences.en: but I wanted to add something.
sentences.zh: 但我希望能留下点什么。

sentences.en: And if that something was that women, Black women, Black people could get paid the equivalent
sentences.zh: 如果这个“什么”是让女性，黑人女性，黑人群体能获得与同行相当的报酬，

sentences.en: of what their counterparts were being paid, I thought that was the thing I could add to.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这就是我能贡献的东西。

sentences.en: That was my legal legacy.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的法律遗产。

sentences.en: And I thought this was my case, you know?
sentences.zh: 我以为这就是我的案子，你懂吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So began the swift, stunted life of United States of America v.
sentences.zh: 于是，“美利坚合众国诉密西西比州参议院”一案，开启了它短暂而受阻的生命。

sentences.en: Mississippi State Senate.
sentences.zh: 诉状里没有任何花哨的技巧。

sentences.en: The complaint didn't have any fancy footwork.
sentences.zh: 我可以肯定地说，这是我读过的最无聊的诉讼之一。

sentences.en: I think I can safely say it's one of the more boring lawsuits I've ever read.
sentences.zh: 它甚至懒得讲一个故事。

sentences.en: It didn't bother to tell a story.
sentences.zh: 它也不需要讲。

sentences.en: It didn't need to.
sentences.zh: 不公平的论点全在数字里。

sentences.zh: 本质上就是克里斯蒂的薪水与她同事薪水的对比清单。

sentences.en: Essentially a rundown of Christy's salary as compared to her colleague's salaries.
sentences.zh: 整个文件只有八页长。

sentences.en: The whole thing is only eight pages long.
sentences.zh: 而第八页只是联系方式。

sentences.en: And the eighth page is just people's contact information.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上只有七页。

sentences.en: So really seven pages.
sentences.zh: 这类案件通常以和解告终。

sentences.en: Cases like these usually end in a settlement.
sentences.zh: 这也是政府对克里斯蒂案的期望。

sentences.en: And that was the government's hope for Christy's case.
sentences.zh: 司法部的一位出庭律师路易斯·惠特塞特向克里斯蒂解释了这一切。

sentences.en: A DOJ trial attorney named Louis Whitsett explained all this to Christy.
sentences.zh: 路易斯告诉我，他觉得我的案子非常棒。

sentences.en: Louis told me that he felt like I had a great case.
sentences.zh: 但就像好莱坞一样，在华盛顿特区也是如此。

sentences.en: But as in Hollywood, so too in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 时机就是一切。

sentences.en: Timing is everything.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂的案子是在2024年11月8日提交的。

sentences.en: Christy's case was filed November 8, 2024.
sentences.zh: 就在唐纳德·特朗普赢得总统大选几天后。

sentences.en: Just a few days after Donald Trump won the presidential election.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几个月里，密西西比州总检察长办公室一直在拖延。

sentences.en: Over the next couple months, the Mississippi AG's office slow-rolled.
sentences.zh: 要求延期回复司法部的诉状。

sentences.en: Asking for extensions to respond to the DOJ complaint.
sentences.zh: 好像他们比司法部的律师更早预见到了这一切的走向。

sentences.en: Like they saw where all this was going before the DOJ lawyers did.
sentences.zh: 也许你也看出了事情的走向。

sentences.en: Maybe you also see where this is going.
sentences.zh: 但以防你没看出来。

sentences.en: But in case you don't.
sentences.zh: 特朗普上任两天后，他的政府冻结了所有新的民权诉讼。

sentences.en: Two days after Trump took office, his administration put a freeze on any new civil rights litigation.
sentences.zh: 并计划审查过去几个月内提交的所有案件，包括克里斯蒂的案子。

sentences.en: And plan to review any cases filed within the past few months, including Christy's.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州在问司法部，所以这个案子被搁置了，对吧？

sentences.en: Mississippi was asking the DOJ, so this case is on ice, right?
sentences.zh: 暂时中止了？

sentences.en: It's stayed for now?
sentences.zh: 而来自民权司的路易斯·惠特塞特反复说，不，没有。

sentences.en: And Louis Whitsett from the Civil Rights Division was saying repeatedly, no, it's not.
sentences.zh: 没有中止。

sentences.en: There's no stay.
sentences.zh: 是的，新领导层确实在审查克里斯蒂的案子，但这并不完全出人意料，甚至不值得惊慌。

sentences.en: Yes, the new bosses were reviewing Christy's case, but that wasn't totally unexpected or even alarming.
sentences.zh: 每一届新政府都会进行评估，推动自己的优先事项。

sentences.en: Every new administration takes stock, pushes its own priorities.
sentences.zh: 但克里斯蒂的案子看起来并不脆弱。

sentences.en: But Christy's case didn't really seem vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个小案子。

sentences.en: It was such a small case.
sentences.zh: 他们提出的法律论点并不具争议性。

sentences.en: The legal argument they were making wasn't controversial.
sentences.zh: 薪酬问题本身也不是什么敏感话题。

sentences.en: And the pay issue itself wasn't a hot button.
sentences.zh: 例如，它并不涉及对跨性别员工的歧视。

sentences.en: It wasn't about discrimination against a trans employee, for instance.
sentences.zh: 况且，新政府通常是在前端，即案件筛选阶段影响民权诉讼，而不是在中途。

sentences.en: And besides, new administrations usually influence civil rights litigation at the front end, when cases are getting chosen, not midstream.
sentences.zh: 所以克里斯蒂的案子，整洁、扎实、已经启动，看起来很安全。

sentences.en: So Christy's case, tidy, solid, already underway, seemed safe.
sentences.zh: 直到突然之间，它不再安全了。

sentences.en: Until suddenly, it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 去年年初，克里斯蒂接到了司法部律师的电话。

sentences.en: Early last year, Christy got a call from the DOJ attorneys.
sentences.zh: 案件被中止了。

sentences.en: The case was being stayed.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂告诉他们，好的，没关系。

sentences.en: Christy told them, OK, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 只是又一次延期，对吧？

sentences.en: Just another delay, right?
sentences.zh: 然后，大约六周后，又接到了一个电话。

sentences.en: And then, about six weeks later, another call.
sentences.zh: 这次通话非常非常简短，他们说，我们接到指示要撤销你的案子。

sentences.en: And it was very, very short and sweet with them saying, we have been directed to dismiss your case.
sentences.zh: 我的第一个问题是，为什么？

sentences.en: And my first question was, why?
sentences.zh: 因为在我心里，我想的是，我们不久前才谈过，你们告诉我发布了中止令。

sentences.en: Because in my mind, I'm thinking, we just talked not too long ago, and you told me that there was a stay issued.
sentences.zh: 而且我的案子没有被撤销，很多其他人的案子才是不了了之了。

sentences.en: And that my case was not being dismissed, that a lot of other people's cases just went away.
sentences.zh: 那么发生了什么，让我的案子在这一届政府的司法部下曾经符合要求，而现在却不符合了？

sentences.en: So what happened that made my case pass muster at some point under this administration's Department of Justice as to where now, it does not.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们不能告诉你任何其他信息。

sentences.en: And they said, we can't tell you anything else.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂想，即使总统换了，法律也没变，对吧？

sentences.en: Even if the president had changed, Christy thought, I mean, the law hasn't changed, right?
sentences.zh: 第七章依然有效。

sentences.en: Title VII is still a thing.
sentences.zh: 所有这些人都向她确认过，你的证据很清晰，你的案子很扎实。

sentences.en: All these people had confirmed to her, your evidence is clear, your case is solid.
sentences.zh: 那为什么要推翻？

sentences.en: So why the reversal?
sentences.zh: 他们没说。

sentences.en: They weren't saying.
sentences.zh: 我们不能告诉你是因为我们不被允许说，还是因为我们自己都不知道？

sentences.en: We can't tell you because we're not supposed to tell you, or we can't tell you because we don't even know?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们不能告诉你任何其他信息。

sentences.en: Well, we can't tell you anything else.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是哪种情况。

sentences.en: I don't know which one it was.
sentences.zh: 所以我试着想出一些其他问题。

sentences.en: And so I try to come up with some other questions.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们说这就是主要问题，我还是想问为什么？

sentences.en: But if they're saying that that's the main question I have is why?
sentences.zh: 这可以上诉吗？

sentences.en: And is this appealable?
sentences.zh: 你知道，还有别人吗？

sentences.en: You know, is there anybody else?
sentences.zh: 我可以和经理谈谈吗？

sentences.en: Can I talk to a manager?
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种感觉就像是，你们确定吗？

sentences.en: You know, it felt like that of, are you sure?
sentences.zh: 就像，这是你们所有人已经为此工作了近三年的事情，我相信，在那一刻。

sentences.en: Like, this is something you all have been working on for almost three years, I believe, at that point.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我可以要回案卷吗？

sentences.en: And I said, well, can I have the case file?
sentences.zh: 我得到的回答基本上就是你回复任何典型《信息自由法》（FOIA）请求的方式。

sentences.en: And I got an answer that was basically how you would answer any typical FOIA requeSt.
sentences.zh: 她惊呆了。

sentences.en: She was floored.
sentences.zh: 因为我基本上是在失去，我觉得我失去了我的律师。

sentences.en: Because I'm essentially losing, I'm losing my attorneys, I feel like.
sentences.zh: 就像，在我费尽周折找到人代表我之后，我以为我拥有了美国能为这个案子工作的最好的律师。

sentences.en: Like, after I had struggled so much to find somebody to represent me, I thought that I had the best attorneys who were available in America to work on this case.
sentences.zh: 我是说，还能找谁呢？

sentences.en: I mean, who better to get?
sentences.zh: 我想在那一刻，我回家后就哭了。

sentences.en: And I think at that point, I went home for the day and just cried.
sentences.zh: 我当时简直崩溃了。

sentences.en: It was just, I was devastated.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有什么东西死去了。

sentences.en: I felt like something died.
sentences.zh: 那么他们到底为什么要撤诉？

sentences.en: So why did they drop it exactly?
sentences.zh: 我把这个问题抛给了珍·斯威迪什。

sentences.en: I put this question to Jen Swedish.
sentences.zh: 她当时是就业诉讼部门的一名经理。

sentences.en: She was a manager in the employment litigation section at the time.
sentences.zh: 她部门里的其他四个案子都被撤销了，但克里斯蒂的案子又拖了七周。

sentences.en: Four other cases in her section had been dropped, but Christie's had lingered for seven more weeks.
sentences.zh: 当它最终死掉时，珍·斯威迪什告诉我，负责此案的律师们感到困惑，这还是轻描淡写的说法。

sentences.en: When it finally died, Jen Swedish told me the attorneys working on it were confused, to say the leaSt.
sentences.zh: 她说，在特朗普第一任期内，这样的案子本来是没问题的。

sentences.en: Under Trump 1, a case like this would have been fine, she said.
sentences.zh: 所以我问她，发生了什么？

sentences.en: So I asked her, what happened?
sentences.zh: 上层给出的理由是什么？

sentences.en: What was the reason that the higher-ups gave?
sentences.zh: 我相信这可能受到特权保护，很遗憾，我不知道我是否能分享。

sentences.en: I believe that's probably protected by a privilege, and I don't know that I can share it, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 无论他们给出的理由是什么——我理解你现在不方便说出来——你相信那个理由吗？

sentences.en: Whatever the reason they did give, that I understand you're not, it's not proper for you to articulate right now, did you buy it?
sentences.zh: 我认为有两个原因，前台办公室都有可能告诉我们他们为什么要撤销这个案子。

sentences.en: There were two reasons that I think would have both been possible for the front office to tell us as to why they wanted the case dismissed.
sentences.zh: 一个是他们所说的那个。

sentences.en: One was the, what they said.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们所说的是一个肤浅的借口，全是胡扯。

sentences.en: I think what they said was a superficial excuse that was bullshit.
sentences.zh: 而幕后真正发生的事情才是真正的原因。

sentences.en: And what actually happened behind the scenes is the real reason.
sentences.zh: 我不知道幕后到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: I don't know exactly what happened behind the scenes.
sentences.zh: 从与司法部那边几个人交谈中，我能说的最多就是，似乎有来自高层的指令。

sentences.en: The most I can say, from talking to a couple of people from the DOJ side, is that there seemed to have been a directive from on high.
sentences.zh: 也许是密西西比州总检察长办公室的某位高层，联系了司法部的某位高层。

sentences.en: Someone high up in the Mississippi AG's office, maybe, who contacted someone high up in the DOJ.
sentences.zh: 然后那个指令被传达给了就业诉讼部门的老板们。

sentences.en: And that that directive got passed down to the bosses in the employment litigation section.
sentences.zh: 撤掉它。

sentences.en: Drop it.
sentences.zh: 今天就撤。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 我向司法部和密西西比州的官员提交了一大堆《信息自由法》请求，试图弄清楚这件事，但我得到的回应中没有任何内容能解释为什么这个案子会这样结束。

sentences.en: I filed a slew of FOIA requests with DOJ and Mississippi officials to try to figure it out, but nothing I got in return clarified why this one went down.
sentences.zh: 司法部和密西西比州总检察长办公室都拒绝了我的置评请求。

sentences.en: Both the DOJ and the Mississippi AG's office declined my requests for comment.
sentences.zh: 珍在我们的谈话中表现得很克制，所以我看不出来。

sentences.en: Jen was pretty measured in our conversation, so I couldn't tell.
sentences.zh: 当他们发现必须撤诉时，他们感到难过吗？

sentences.en: Were they upset when they found out they had to drop it?
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: All right.

sentences.en: So you didn't have, like, nobody came to your office being like, what the fuck about this case?
sentences.zh: 哦，不，他们有。

sentences.en: Oh, no, they did.
sentences.zh: 哦，他们有。

sentences.en: Oh, they did.
sentences.zh: 哦，他们有。

sentences.en: Oh, they did.
sentences.zh: 哦，我的办公室里对这个案子有太多的情绪了。

sentences.en: Oh, there's so much, there's so much emotion about this case in my office.
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Oh, everyone was so, everyone who was aware of what was happening with this case was really upset about it.
sentences.zh: 哦，每个人都，每个了解这起案件情况的人都对此感到非常难过。

sentences.en: But was there something about this one in particular or no?
sentences.zh: 但这个案子有什么特别之处吗，还是没有？

sentences.en: I think, you know, compared to other cases, I mean, this is a very strong case.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，与其他案件相比，我的意思是，这是一个非常有力的案件。

sentences.en: So to see a very strong case involving a Black woman who was discriminated against, it rang true to us that this administration wouldn't care about vindicating her rights,
sentences.zh: 所以看到一个涉及黑人女性遭受歧视的强有力案件，却让我们觉得本届政府根本不在乎维护她的权利，这让我们感到很真实，

sentences.en: which is really upsetting.
sentences.zh: 这真的让人很沮丧。

sentences.en: One person told me Christie's case wasn't just a strong case.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉我，克里斯蒂的案子不仅仅是一个强有力的案件。

sentences.en: It was the strongest pay discrimination case they'd had in years.
sentences.zh: 这是他们多年来处理过的最强有力的薪酬歧视案。

sentences.en: Having to dismiss it, let her to quit the DOJ.
sentences.zh: 不得不撤诉，让她离开了司法部。

sentences.en: I didn't know you could do that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道还能这样。

sentences.en: I didn't know you could disappear a federal case like this without a defensible reason.
sentences.zh: 我不知道竟然可以这样毫无正当理由地让一起联邦案件消失。

sentences.en: An honorable people can disagree type of reason.
sentences.zh: 那种“正人君子也会有分歧”的理由。

sentences.en: But if it's true that the new civil rights bosses weren't making a decision based on the evidence and the law, then I'm not sure how else to interpret this.
sentences.zh: 但如果新的民权部门负责人确实不是基于证据和法律做出决定，那我就不知道该如何解读这件事了。

sentences.en: Except that they were making a decision based on the color of Christie's skin.
sentences.zh: 只能认为他们是基于克里斯蒂的肤色做出的决定。

sentences.en: When the DOJ first took up Christie's case, she'd heard from all these other women, almost all Black women, not only in Mississippi, but from all over the place,
sentences.zh: 当司法部最初接手克里斯蒂的案子时，她听到了所有其他女性的声音，几乎都是黑人女性，不仅是在密西西比州，而是来自各地，

sentences.en: who had similar stories of unfairness, of being paid less or treated worse, exponents of her own outrage.
sentences.zh: 她们都有着类似的遭遇，关于不公平，关于薪酬更低或待遇更差，她们是她愤怒的共鸣者。

sentences.en: Now that her case was dropped, the messages came again.
sentences.zh: 现在她的案子被撤销了，这些信息又来了。

sentences.en: I started getting what I'm going to call condolence messages from friends, classmates who were aware of the lawsuit being filed on my behalf.
sentences.zh: 我开始收到我称之为慰问的信息，来自那些知道我提起诉讼的朋友和同学。

sentences.en: And that made it worse because I felt like I was letting all of these people down who were rooting for me.
sentences.zh: 这让情况变得更糟，因为我觉得我辜负了所有支持我的人。

sentences.en: After a couple weeks, she rallied.
sentences.zh: 几周后，她振作了起来。

sentences.en: And I just, I finally realized, well, I didn't dismiss my case.
sentences.zh: 我终于意识到，好吧，我并没有撤诉。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I didn't quit.
sentences.zh: 我没有放弃。

sentences.en: They quit on me.
sentences.zh: 是他们放弃了我。

sentences.en: For whatever reason.
sentences.zh: 不管出于什么原因。

sentences.en: And I've got to figure out something else.
sentences.zh: 我得想点别的办法。

sentences.en: Within a month, Christie had found a private law firm to file a new Title VII lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 不到一个月，克里斯蒂就找到了一家私人律师事务所，提起了一项新的第七章诉讼。

sentences.en: She's not giving up.
sentences.zh: 她没有放弃。

sentences.en: She has other updates, too.
sentences.zh: 她还有其他更新。

sentences.en: Her private life is good.
sentences.zh: 她的私生活很好。

sentences.en: She's reconnected with her stepchildren, and they're doing great.
sentences.zh: 她和继子女们重新建立了联系，他们相处得很好。

sentences.en: She's working as an attorney for the Mississippi Department of Health.
sentences.zh: 她现在在密西西比州卫生部担任律师。

sentences.en: I review contracts for communicable diseases, IT for health administration, epidemiology.
sentences.zh: 我负责审查传染病、卫生管理信息技术、流行病学方面的合同。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's very boring.
sentences.zh: 非常无聊。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: It's okay, though.
sentences.zh: 不过没关系。

sentences.en: It's not okay.
sentences.zh: 这可不好。

sentences.en: Christie Metcalfe is rare.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂·梅特卡夫是个稀有人物。

sentences.en: An optimistic person.
sentences.zh: 一个乐观的人。

sentences.en: A can-do person who is also not naive.
sentences.zh: 一个既能干又不天真的人。

sentences.en: She knows history.
sentences.zh: 她了解历史。

sentences.en: She knows how things tend to shake out in this country for Black women from rural Alabama.
sentences.zh: 她知道在这个国家，来自阿拉巴马州农村的黑人女性通常会面临什么样的结局。

sentences.en: And yet she's not a cynic.
sentences.zh: 然而她并不是一个愤世嫉俗者。

sentences.en: She's a believer in hard work.
sentences.zh: 她相信努力工作。

sentences.en: And the idea that even if you have to work twice as hard, it's worth it.
sentences.zh: 并且相信即使你必须付出双倍的努力，这也是值得的。

sentences.en: An idea a lot of us rely on.
sentences.zh: 一个我们许多人都依赖的信念。

sentences.en: Take that belief away.
sentences.zh: 如果剥夺了这种信念。

sentences.en: What are you left with?
sentences.zh: 你还剩下什么？

sentences.en: Sorry, you're saying you've kind of just, like, stopped trying as hard?
sentences.zh: 抱歉，你是说你有点，就像，不再那么努力了吗？

sentences.en: Is that what you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是这个意思吗？

sentences.en: I hate to admit that, but that's what it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我不想承认，但确实是这样，是的。

sentences.en: Because you've a little bit lost faith in the notion of a reward for hard work.
sentences.zh: 因为你对努力工作会有回报这一观念失去了一点信心。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: For now, at least, the Mississippi State Senate doesn't have to change its hiring or pay practices, discriminatory or not.
sentences.zh: 至少目前，密西西比州参议院不必改变其招聘或薪酬做法，无论是否具有歧视性。

sentences.en: Looking back at that list of cases where I first saw Christie's lawsuit, the same is true all over the country.
sentences.zh: 回顾我最初看到克里斯蒂诉讼的那份案件清单，全国各地的情况都是如此。

sentences.en: The South Bend, Indiana, Police Department.
sentences.zh: 印第安纳州南本德警察局。

sentences.en: The Maryland State Police.
sentences.zh: 马里兰州州警。

sentences.en: The fire departments in Durham, North Carolina and Cobb County, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 北卡罗来纳州达勒姆和佐治亚州科布县的消防部门。

sentences.en: All employment cases that the DOJ has disavowed or dropped.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是司法部否认或撤销的就业案件。

sentences.en: And cases regarding alleged workplace discrimination against transgender people?
sentences.zh: 还有关于针对跨性别者职场歧视的指控案件？

sentences.en: Definitely not.
sentences.zh: 绝对没有。

sentences.en: A hotel chain in New York.
sentences.zh: 纽约的一家连锁酒店。

sentences.en: A Wendy's franchise in Florida.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州的一家温蒂汉堡加盟店。

sentences.en: Lush Cosmetics.
sentences.zh: Lush化妆品公司。

sentences.en: A pig farming operation in Illinois.
sentences.zh: 伊利诺伊州的一家养猪场。

sentences.en: A pizza place at O'Hare.
sentences.zh: 奥黑尔机场的一家披萨店。

sentences.en: Culver's Restaurants in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 密歇根州的Culver's餐厅。

sentences.en: All places where the EEOC initially found Title VII violations prior to Trump's election.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是在特朗普当选前，平等就业机会委员会（EEOC）最初认定存在违反第七章行为的地方。

sentences.en: Post-election, the EEOC backed away from every single one.
sentences.zh: 选举后，EEOC对每一个案件都退缩了。

sentences.en: When I talked to Jen Swedish, she told me she'd been one of 10 people on the employment litigation management team for the Civil Rights Division.
sentences.zh: 当我与简·斯威迪什交谈时，她告诉我她是民权部门就业诉讼管理团队的10人之一。

sentences.en: Soon after she left, there was only one person left on that team.
sentences.zh: 她离开后不久，该团队就只剩下一人了。

sentences.en: In late December of 2024, the section had between 30 and 40 trial attorneys on staff.
sentences.zh: 2024年12月底，该部门有30到40名出庭律师。

sentences.en: By the end of last year, there were 11.
sentences.zh: 到去年年底，只剩下11人。

sentences.en: And that's just employment litigation.
sentences.zh: 而这仅仅是就业诉讼。

sentences.en: Voting, housing, disability rights.
sentences.zh: 投票权、住房、残疾人权利。

sentences.en: By all accounts, the whole Civil Rights Division has been gutted.
sentences.zh: 据各方说法，整个民权部门已经被掏空了。

sentences.en: The latest number I saw was that about 75 percent of the DOJ's civil rights attorneys are gone.
sentences.zh: 我看到的最新数字是，大约75%的司法部民权律师已经离职。

sentences.en: Christy Metcalf's personal discrimination lawsuit, the one she filed last year on her own in federal court.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂·梅特卡夫的个人歧视诉讼，就是她去年自己向联邦法院提起的那个案子。

sentences.en: As of right now, the case has been stayed, meaning it's on hold.
sentences.zh: 截至目前，该案已被中止，意味着处于搁置状态。

sentences.en: Pending a decision on a motion filed by lawyers for the Mississippi State Senate, they're asking the judge to dismiss the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 等待密西西比州参议院律师提交的一项动议的裁决，他们要求法官驳回整个案件。

sentences.zh: 以上是来自Serial Productions的莎拉·凯尼格。

sentences.zh: 一定要收看Serial的新节目《白痴》，作者是M。

sentences.en: Gessen.
sentences.zh: 格森。

sentences.zh: 本月晚些时候播出。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 前往nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的事情。

sentences.en: A Senate vote to reopen the Department of Homeland Security failed on Thursday,
sentences.zh: 周四，参议院关于重开国土安全部的投票失败了，

sentences.en: as Democrats continue to refuse backing a funding bill without significant new restrictions on federal immigration officers.
sentences.zh: 因为民主党人继续拒绝在没有对联邦移民官员进行重大新限制的情况下支持拨款法案。

sentences.en: Thousands of federal workers have gone without paychecks since the shutdown began on February 14th, including at TSA,
sentences.zh: 自2月14日政府停摆开始以来，数千名联邦工作人员一直没有领到工资，包括运输安全管理局（TSA）的员工，

sentences.en: with experts warning that scattered backups at airport security around the country could become more frequent.
sentences.zh: 专家警告称，全国各地机场安检处零星出现的积压可能会变得更加频繁。

sentences.en: Border control and immigration enforcement agencies, meanwhile, are operating with money approved separately by Republicans last year.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，边境管制和移民执法机构正在使用共和党人去年单独批准的资金运作。

sentences.en: And a driver rammed a truck into a synagogue outside Detroit on Thursday, raising further alarm about rising anti-Semitism in America.
sentences.zh: 周四，一名司机驾驶卡车冲进了底特律郊外的一座犹太教堂，引发了对美国反犹太主义抬头进一步的担忧。

sentences.en: Sheriff Michael Bouchard of Oakland County said the suspect drove through the doors and down the hall of Temple Israel in West Bloomfield Township.
sentences.zh: 奥克兰县警长迈克尔·布沙尔表示，嫌疑人开车穿过了西布卢姆菲尔德镇以色列会堂的大门并沿着走廊行驶。

sentences.en: A fire started in the building, and the sheriff described video footage that showed the attacker, quote, traveling with purpose through the hallway.
sentences.zh: 大楼内起火，警长描述了视频片段，显示袭击者“有目的地在走廊中穿行”。

sentences.en: The attacker died after an exchange of gunfire with security guards.
sentences.zh: 袭击者在与保安交火后死亡。

sentences.en: The 140 students at the synagogue's preschool were unhurt, according to Temple Israel officials.
sentences.zh: 据以色列会堂官员称，犹太教堂幼儿园的140名学生没有受伤。

sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
